memories.content: The user stores copies of identity documents in an encrypted folder.
On a day the user transferred between buses twice, they rested for an hour after the trip.
On a day the user took a direct route with a similar travel time, they remained seated to the destination.
After arriving at an entrance with stairs only, the user went around to an entrance on the other side of the building.
On a day the user checked the accessible entrance location in advance, they arrived before the agreed time.
On a rainy day, the user's clothes became wet while crossing an uncovered section at a transfer stop.
On a day the user traveled with their maternal uncle, they agreed to meet at an entrance near the elevator.
The user's maternal uncle prefers an aisle seat from which it is easy to stand during long-distance travel.
The local agent cannot know whether an accessible entrance is operating that day from past route records alone.
The transfer route the user takes has more boarding and alighting events and walking segments than the direct route.
The user stores tax-related receipts in digital folders by year.
The user found three paper receipts late and recalculated the expense total already prepared.
Starting the next month, the user photographed receipts on the day they were received and reduced omissions.
The user named every file with only the photo date and spent a long time looking for a needed receipt.
The user later included the expense category in the filename and found the receipt immediately through search.
While reviewing documents just before submission, the user discovered one blank signature field.
Before submitting an administrative document, the user checks the signature field as the final item on the checklist.
Staff at a tax-support counter expect to receive an electronic copy in which every item is legible rather than a blurred or cropped photo.
The local agent can organize receipts by date and category but cannot determine whether an expense is deductible.
The accepted scope and submission deadlines for administrative documents may vary under that year's guidance.

analysis.overview: The frames address separate operational areas rather than competing guidance. The reference describes document security, travel effort, accessibility, weather exposure, coordination, seating preference, and route-data limits; the compared frame describes receipt management, submission checks, document quality, agent limits, and changing administrative guidance.

relations.reason: This is independently useful security information, with no claim in the compared frame about protecting identity documents or encrypting stored files.
relations.summary: Identity-document copies are kept in an encrypted folder.

relations.reason: These memories jointly describe the one-sided operational distinction between transfer and direct travel burden; the compared frame contains no travel-routing claim.
relations.summary: Compared with a similarly timed direct trip, the transfer route involved more physical transitions, while the observed direct trip allowed continuous sitting and the transfer trip was followed by rest.

relations.reason: This is a specific accessibility workaround absent from the compared frame.
relations.summary: When confronted with a stairs-only entrance, the user navigated to another side of the building for an alternative entrance.

relations.reason: This is independently useful evidence about advance accessibility planning, with no counterpart in the compared frame.
relations.summary: Checking the accessible entrance location beforehand coincided with arriving before the agreed time.

relations.reason: This travel-weather exposure is not addressed by any compared-frame memory.
relations.summary: An uncovered section at a transfer stop exposed the user to rain and wet clothing.

relations.reason: This is a specific travel-coordination and accessibility detail absent from the compared frame.
relations.summary: While traveling with their maternal uncle, the user arranged to meet at an entrance near the elevator.

relations.reason: This personal seating preference is independently useful and has no compared-frame counterpart.
relations.summary: The user's maternal uncle prefers an aisle seat that makes standing easier on long-distance trips.

relations.reason: This defines a route-planning knowledge limit distinct from the compared frame's different administrative judgment limits.
relations.summary: Past route records alone cannot establish whether an accessible entrance is operating on a particular day.

relations.reason: This filing practice concerns tax receipts and yearly organization, neither of which appears in the reference frame.
relations.summary: Tax-related receipts are organized in digital folders by year.

relations.reason: The memories form a single before-and-after claim about same-day receipt capture reducing omissions and rework; the reference frame contains no receipt-capture practice.
relations.summary: Late discovery of paper receipts caused recalculation, while photographing receipts when received subsequently reduced omissions.

relations.reason: The memories jointly express one filename-specificity claim about receipt retrieval, with no corresponding reference-frame policy.
relations.summary: Date-only filenames hindered receipt retrieval, whereas adding the expense category enabled immediate search-based retrieval.

relations.reason: These memories jointly describe one submission-checking safeguard absent from the reference frame.
relations.summary: Discovery of a blank signature field prompted a practice of checking the signature field last before administrative submission.

relations.reason: This external document-quality expectation has no reference-frame counterpart.
relations.summary: Tax-support staff expect an electronic copy in which every item is legible rather than blurred or cropped.

relations.reason: This defines a tax-specific boundary between clerical organization and substantive judgment, distinct from the reference frame's route-status limitation.
relations.summary: The local agent may organize receipts by date and category but cannot determine expense deductibility.

relations.reason: This time-sensitive administrative constraint is independently useful and absent from the reference frame.
relations.summary: Accepted scope and submission deadlines for administrative documents may vary with the year's guidance.

reports.compared_only: Compared-only material concerns tax-receipt capture, organization and retrieval, signature checks, legible electronic submissions, limits on deductibility judgments, and year-specific administrative rules and deadlines.
reports.reference_only: Reference-only material concerns encrypted identity-document storage and practical travel accessibility, including transfer burden, entrance planning, weather exposure, meeting arrangements, seating preferences, and limits of historical route data.
